task:
FIX A REAL CI FAILURE ON PR #817 (purge P1, migration 016). Update only the existing branch codex/run-38689108057-1; its head must be 79d1696caf2fc7555a144c5a6fb7cee026420333 (full SHA from git rev-parse of origin/codex/run-38689108057-1; if it differs, stop and report the SHA you found). Read CLAUDE.md, docs/development/v3-governed-derived-purge-design.md section 4.1 item 4 (the executor role), sql/v3/migrations/016_v3_governed_derived_purge.sql lines 1-45, and tests/test_v3_governed_derived_purge.py lines 40-160.

THE FAILURE (CI lane "Finder derived-data tests (PostgreSQL 18)", >50 failures): PostgreSQL roles are CLUSTER-wide, but the CI fixtures create a fresh database per test on ONE server. 016 runs an unconditional `CREATE ROLE v3_derived_purge_executor`, so after the first test database applies the full manifest, every later 016 application on that server fails with role-already-exists, and tests/test_v3_governed_derived_purge.py:88 then asserts the role is absent ("test refuses to adopt existing cluster role"). The same happens on any real server that hosts more than one database applying this lineage (a Review Lab or rehearsal database beside another). Fix it in the migration, not by weakening tests.

THE FIX (fail-closed adoption): in 016, create the role only if it does not exist (`CREATE ROLE` inside a DO block guarded by pg_roles, still immediately preceded by `SET LOCAL createrole_self_grant = 'set'`). If it already exists, ADOPT it only after verifying, and otherwise raise: rolcanlogin false, rolsuper false, rolcreaterole false, rolcreatedb false, rolreplication false, rolbypassrls false, rolinherit false, rolconnlimit -1 or 0, no password (rolpassword null via pg_authid only if readable; if not readable, skip that one check and say so), the role is a member of NO other role (no pg_auth_members row with member = the executor), and the creating role holds membership in it with set_option true and inherit_option false (when the existing role was created by the same non-superuser creator in another database this membership already exists; if it is missing and the creator is not superuser, raise -- do not try to GRANT it, design 4.1 explains why that is not possible). Superuser creators keep the existing skip of the membership assertion. Keep every per-database GRANT/REVOKE in the migration (they are per-database and must run in each database). Then, in tests/test_v3_governed_derived_purge.py, replace the "refuses to adopt existing cluster role" precondition with: the test runs correctly whether or not the cluster already has the role (create the application role edfinder_v3 only if absent, and never DROP a cluster role another database still depends on -- only drop roles this test created and only after DROP OWNED in this test's database, tolerating dependencies in other databases by skipping the drop). Add NEW tests: (a) applying 016 to a second database on the same cluster succeeds and adopts the role; (b) an existing role named v3_derived_purge_executor with LOGIN (or SUPERUSER-free but with INHERIT, or a membership in another role) makes 016 fail closed with a clear message and leaves the database unchanged (the migration is one transaction). Make sure every other PG18 test module that applies the full manifest keeps passing when run in the same session after the purge tests and before them.

ALLOWED FILES: sql/v3/migrations/016_v3_governed_derived_purge.sql; sql/v3/migration-manifest.txt (the 016 hash changes); deploy/v3-production/target-authority.json (regenerated identity only, via scripts/operator/v3_schema_identity.py, plus the evidence text's checksum/identity values); tests/test_v3_governed_derived_purge.py; any test that pins the 016 hash or the regenerated identity (update, list each); CHANGES.md. Nothing else.

VALIDATION TO RUN AND REPORT WITH EXACT COUNTS: ruff check scripts tests; python -m pytest tests/test_v3_lineage_migrations.py tests/test_v3_production_migration_operation.py tests/test_v3_production_application_deployment.py tests/test_v3_release_gate_f2d.py tests/test_v3_governed_derived_purge.py -q -p no:warnings (PG18 ones skip on the runner: list them as written-not-run); validate_authority on deploy/v3-production/target-authority.json (expect []); the new migration-set identity and target checksum. End with: files changed; the exact adoption checks implemented; tests with counts; anything you could not do.
